form.audienceTooltip: The resource identifier this server is registered as at your identity provider. Exchanged tokens are scoped to it.

sheet.persistentConnectionHelp: Enable to keep one shared connection open and reused across every caller. Disable to connect fresh on every call instead.

sheet.toolExecutionTimeoutHelp: Override the global tool execution timeout for this server. Leave empty or set to 0 to use the global setting.

sessions.title: MCP Auth Sessions
sessions.description: Per-user credentials stored for MCP servers (OAuth tokens and submitted headers), plus any pending authentication flows.
sessions.empty: No sessions yet. Sessions appear here when an inference request or MCP gateway call triggers per-user authentication (OAuth or header submission).

tooltips.type: OAuth: per-user OAuth credential, either a stored token from a completed sign-in, or a pending sign-in flow. Headers: per-user header values (API keys / signed tokens), either stored or pending submission.
tooltips.boundTo: The identity this credential is keyed to: an end user (via SSO), a virtual key (shared by anyone using that VK), or a client-issued session ID (asserted via the x-bf-mcp-session-id header).
tooltips.status: Active: credential valid and usable. Pending: OAuth flow in progress, user must complete sign-in. Needs re-auth: upstream credential expired or revoked at the provider; user must reconnect. Needs update: the admin changed the required header keys; user must resubmit. Orphaned: the user lost access to this MCP (e.g. an access profile change); credential is preserved and will become Active automatically if access is restored.
tooltips.accessTokenExpiry: When the current access token expires. Bifrost auto-refreshes using the refresh token on the next request, so an active row past its expiry will silently mint a new token at use time. Header rows do not have an upstream expiry; their values stay valid until revoked or the schema changes.

sessions.revokeHeaderDescription: Bifrost will remove the stored credential values for this binding. There is no upstream token to revoke; the user will need to resubmit their header values to use this MCP again.
sessions.revokeSessionDescription: Bifrost will remove the stored credential for this binding. The upstream OAuth token is not revoked at the provider; it stays detached and expires naturally. Anyone using this binding will need to re-authenticate to obtain a fresh token.
sessions.scopesHelp: Scopes the provider granted at sign-in, as reported in its token response. Shown as a dash when the provider did not report them. Header submissions and pending sign-ins have no scopes.
sessions.refreshTokenHelp: Whether the provider issued a refresh token. Present: Bifrost renews the access token automatically at use time. Not issued: the row must be re-authenticated once the access token expires. Rejected upstream: the provider refused the last refresh, so the row needs re-auth. Header rows and pending sign-ins have no token.

auth.missingFlowBody: This URL is missing the flow query parameter. Open the link from your inference response or the sessions tab.
auth.notYoursBody: The pending flow belongs to a different identity. Ask the teammate whose VK or user identity triggered the original request to complete it, or trigger a new request yourself.
auth.expiredTitle: This authentication flow has expired or been completed
auth.expiredBody: Pending flows expire after a short window. If you still need to authenticate, trigger the original action again so a fresh flow is created.
auth.loadFailedTitle: Could not load this authentication flow
auth.replaceBody: An active credential already exists for the binding below. Completing this flow will replace it with a fresh credential. You can also close this tab to keep using the existing one.
auth.redirectBody: You'll be redirected to the provider to sign in and grant access. Bifrost stores the resulting credential against the binding below so this request and future ones can proceed automatically.
auth.headersSavedBody: Bifrost verified the connection and stored your credentials. You can close this tab and retry the original action.
auth.submissionExpiredTitle: This submission link has expired or been used
auth.submissionExpiredBody: Submission flows expire after a short window. Trigger the original request again to get a fresh link.
auth.submissionLoadFailed: Could not load this submission link
auth.replaceHeaders: This server already has stored credentials for you. Submitting new values replaces the existing entry; the server will be re-verified before saving.
auth.supplyKeys: This server requires you to supply your own API keys / tokens. The values you submit are stored encrypted and only used to authenticate your own requests.
auth.flowNoLonger: This authentication flow can no longer be completed
auth.alreadyStored: The OAuth credential for {{name}} is already stored. You can close this tab.
auth.triggerAgain: Trigger the original action again so a fresh flow is created.
auth.invalidLinkTitle: This authentication link is no longer valid
auth.invalidLinkBody: The link may have expired, been used already, invalid, or had its short-lived token stripped. Trigger the original action again so a fresh authentication link is created.
auth.successBody: Your credential has been stored. You can close this tab and return to your MCP client - future requests will use this credential automatically.
auth.failedFallback: We couldn't complete the authentication flow.
auth.failedHint: You can close this tab and retry the original request from your MCP client to generate a fresh authentication link.

oauthGrants.title: OAuth Grants
oauthGrants.description: Active downstream OAuth grants issued to MCP clients that connected via the OAuth consent flow.

tooltips.boundTo: The identity this grant is tied to: an end user (via SSO), a virtual key (shared by anyone using that VK), or an anonymous session. This determines which upstream per-user OAuth sessions are reachable under this grant.
tooltips.accessTokenExpiry: When the current JWT access token expires. MCP clients silently refresh using the refresh token, so an active grant past its expiry will mint a new token automatically on the next request.
tooltips.lastUsed: When this grant last refreshed its access token. MCP clients refresh as their token nears expiry, so this tracks the grant's most recent activity. Grants that have not refreshed since they were authorized fall back to when they were created.

oauthGrants.revokeDescription: The refresh token for this grant stops rotating right away, so the MCP client can no longer renew its access. Its current access token is a short-lived JWT that keeps working on the /mcp endpoint until it expires (default 10 minutes), after which the client is fully cut off and must reconnect via the OAuth consent flow.
